pages.title: What Is Waste?
pages.content:
Every day, we buy food in boxes. We drink water from plastic or glass bottles. Sometimes we do not eat all our food, so we throw it away. These boxes, bottles and food are not the only waste. Everything we throw away is waste. The world is big, but these things are not forever. So, we should not waste our food and items.

There is a lot of waste in the world. In 2023, people in cities made more than 2 billion tons of waste. In 2050, there will be about 4 billion tons!

There is a lot of waste, but it is not all trash. We can use it again.

vocabulary.definition: Put something in the bin.
Things we do not want or need.
For all time; with no end.
Things, like boxes, bottles or clothes.
1 ton is 1,000 kilograms.
Things with no use; we cannot use them again.

pages.title: Paper, Wood and Glass
pages.content:
Paper and wood come from trees. We can recycle old paper. Then we can make new paper and new boxes. This is good for the world.

We can make new things from used wood, too. For example, old tables and chairs go to recycling factories. There, workers make new home items from them.

We should put old glass bottles and jars in a recycling bin. Recycling workers take them. They put green, brown and white glass in different groups. Then, they make new bottles and jars.

pages.title: Plastic and the Sea
pages.content:
Plastic is in many things. Bags, bottles, pens and phones have plastic in them.

In 2019, there were about 350 million tons of plastic waste in the world. People recycled only 9 percent of it. People put half of it under the ground. And people threw a lot of it into rivers and the sea. Plastic in rivers and the sea is a big problem. Fish and birds eat it, and they get ill. Plastic also makes the water dirty. We shouldn’t throw plastic into rivers and the sea.

pages.title: Cartons, Cans and Oil
pages.content:
Juice and milk cartons have paper and plastic in them. Workers at the recycling factory separate the paper and the plastic. Then they make new products.

Drink cans are metal. They are not trash, either. Recycling workers melt used metal and make new things from it.

Another problem is waste oil. After we cook food, we have used oil. It is waste, too. We mustn’t put it into the sink. It makes the water dirty.

pages.title: Food Waste
pages.content:
A lot of food goes to waste. We throw away food at home, in restaurants and in shops. But where is the biggest problem? It is at home! 61 percent of all food waste comes from our homes. We buy too much food, and then we cannot eat it.

We should buy only the food that we need. For example, we should eat the bread from yesterday first.

pages.title: Old Phones and Batteries
pages.content:
We have a lot of machines at home and at school. We use phones, computers and TVs every day. Sometimes they get old or break, so we throw them away.

We should put old machines in a recycling bin. Recycling workers take them from these bins. Then they bring them to recycling factories. There, they separate the metal and plastic pieces to use them again.

Batteries make games, phones and clocks work. Old batteries are dangerous. We mustn’t throw them in the kitchen bin. We should put old batteries in a battery bin.

pages.title: Zero Waste and the Three Rs
pages.content:
What is Zero Waste? It is not “no waste”. Every person makes some waste every day. Zero Waste is less waste. We can use items and products again and again.

Here are the three Rs of Zero Waste:

Reduce: Use less. Buy only the things that you need.

Reuse and Repair: Use products again. When something is broken, repair it.

Recycle: Make new things from old things.

Old items can become new products again.

pages.title: What Can We Do?
pages.content:
The best waste is no waste! We can all help the world. For example, we can take a bag from home to the shop. At school, we can use our own bottles and cups. We should also say “no” to plastic straws.

Cities can help, too. Some cities have tool libraries. People can take tools from there, and they do not need to buy them.

Families can learn about Zero Waste together. The best time to start is now!

terms.definition: A way of life with less waste.
Make new things from old things.
terms.definitionAr: صُنْعُ أَشْيَاءَ جَدِيدَةٍ مِنْ أَشْيَاءَ قَدِيمَةٍ.

terms.definition: Use less. Buy only the things that you need.
terms.definitionAr: أَنْ نَسْتَخْدِمَ أَقَلَّ، وَأَلَّا نَشْتَرِيَ إِلَّا مَا نَحْتَاجُ إِلَيْهِ.

terms.definition: A box for things that we can recycle.
terms.definitionAr: صُنْدُوقٌ لِلْأَشْيَاءِ الَّتِي يُمْكِنُ إِعَادَةُ تَدْوِيرِهَا.

terms.definitionAr: مَكَانٌ يَأْخُذُ مِنْهُ النَّاسُ الْأَدَوَاتِ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُونَهَا.

pages.title: Language Review
pages.content: Review the language from all chapters.

exercises.title: Look: Should, Shouldn’t, Mustn’t
exercises.question: Which word goes in the gap?

formChoices.sentence: We [choice] buy only the food that we need.
We [choice] throw plastic into rivers and the sea.
We [choice] put used oil into the sink.

exercises.explanation: Should = it is good to do it. Shouldn’t = it is not good to do it. Mustn’t = do not do it.

feedback.incorrect: Find these sentences in Chapters 3, 4 and 5.

exercises.title: Practise: Which Bin?
exercises.instructions: Put each thing in the right group.
exercises.question: Where does it go?

items: old glass jars
old paper
old phones
old batteries

exercises.explanation: Chapter 2: glass and paper. Chapter 6: old machines go in a recycling bin, old batteries go in a battery bin.

feedback.incorrect: Read Chapters 2 and 6 again.

exercises.title: Practise: Then and Now
exercises.question: Past or now?

formChoices.sentence: In 2019, there [choice] about 350 million tons of plastic waste.

exercises.explanation: In 2019 = the past: were, recycled. Today = now: is.

feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 3 again.

exercises.title: Practise: The Best, The Biggest
exercises.instructions: Fill the gaps with the words.
exercises.question: Which word goes in the gap?
exercises.fillBlanksText: Where is the [blank] problem? It is at home! The [blank] waste is no waste! The best time to start is [blank]!
exercises.explanation: Big → the biggest. Good → the best.

feedback.incorrect: Find these sentences in Chapters 5 and 8.

exercises.title: Practise: Fix One Word
exercises.instructions: Find the wrong word. Choose the right word.
exercises.question: Which word is wrong?

errorItems.sentence: People throwed a lot of it into rivers.
Every person make some waste every day.

exercises.explanation: Throw changes in the past: threw. Every person = one: makes.

feedback.incorrect: Throw → threw. One person + verb + -s.

exercises.title: Use: Our Zero Waste Class
exercises.instructions: Write three sentences: a Zero Waste class.
exercises.question: What can our class do?
exercises.explanation: Use should, mustn’t and a “Do this!” sentence.

discussionPrompts.question: One “should”: “We should …”
discussionPrompts.example: We should use our own bottles.

discussionPrompts.question: One “mustn’t”: “We mustn’t …”
discussionPrompts.example: We mustn’t throw batteries in the bin.

discussionPrompts.question: One “Do this!” sentence: “Use … / Buy … / Repair …”
discussionPrompts.example: Repair old books.

exercises.question: Why are tool libraries good?
options: People do not need to buy tools.

feedback.correct: Yes. People do not need to buy tools.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 8.

exercises.title: The Life of a Can
exercises.question: What comes first?

sequencingItems.text: We drink juice from a can.
We put the can in a recycling bin.
The workers make new things from the metal.

exercises.explanation: Chapter 4: “Recycling workers melt used metal and make new things from it.”

feedback.correct: Great! A can is not trash.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 4.
